subject: Post-call: FintechAI pricing & latency trade-offs

Subject: Post-call: FintechAI pricing & latency trade-offs

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned:

Call recap:
- Primary use: customer-facing conversational assistants (core flows) + embeddings for search/rerank.
- Expected steady-state volumes: you mentioned ~20M generative tokens/month (peak patterns around business hours), and ~3M embedding tokens/month.
- Latency SLO: core flows need low p95 (you said target <250ms for primary UIs). Some async/background flows can tolerate ~1s.

Immediate asks / items I need to finalize a proposal:
1) Confirm monthly token volumes (generative / embeddings / rerank) and any monthly seasonality (e.g., 2x spikes).
2) Target monthly budget range for inference spend (ballpark helps us pick hosted vs dedicated).
3) Confirm whether <250ms p95 is strict for all user journeys or only the top N flows.

What I’ll send by EOD Monday:
- Two configuration options (Hosted low-latency tier vs Dedicated reserved capacity) with estimated $/1M token math and commit implications.
- Recommended batching/streaming settings and expected latency vs unit-cost trade-offs.

Proposed next step: 30-min touch on Wed to review options and procurement path. Are you available Wed 6/30 10am PT?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.example.com | +1 415-555-0147

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Volumes: after double-checking with product, best estimate is ~20M generative tokens/month (user-facing), ~3M embeddings/month, and ~1M rerank tokens. We do see weekday daytime peaks (~1.8x).
- Budget: procurement is expecting to see options in the $8k–$12k/mo range for the initial phase; if Dedicated requires large commits we need to see clear unit-cost wins to justify.
- Latency: <250ms p95 is a hard requirement for the top-3 user journeys (login flows, statement generation, fraud-check helper). The other flows can be 400–1000ms.

I uploaded procurement contact details to the cc’d mailbox and we can loop them in once we have a price band. Also, please send any benchmarking numbers you have for 250ms p95 at those volumes.

Wed 6/30 10am PT works for me — sending a calendar invite.

Subject: Re: Post-call: FintechAI pricing & latency trade-offs

Daniel —

Thanks for confirming. I’ve attached a quick pricing math workbook (redwood-pricing-math.xlsx) and a short benchmark summary. High-level options below — I’ll walk through these on Wed:

Option A — Hosted (Low-latency tier)
- Pros: no commit, fast onboarding, we can guarantee low-latency SLOs on the low-latency tier with burst capacity.
- Cons: higher unit cost.
- Ballpark unit economics: ~$28 / 1M tokens (generative) at the volumes you quoted, assuming low-latency tier + streaming.
- Fit if you need zero-commit and want to test in prod quickly.

Option B — Dedicated (Reserved capacity)
- Pros: significantly lower unit cost at committed capacity, more predictable p95 latency at scale, data isolation.
- Cons: commit required (we can discuss 6–12 month terms), operational onboarding.
- Ballpark unit economics: ~$11–$13 / 1M tokens (generative) with a 12-month reserved plan and typical batching/kv-cache optimizations.

Latency vs cost notes (short):
- Streaming: recommended for user-facing flows; gives lower perceived latency because tokens stream as they’re generated. Slightly higher per-token compute due to less batching but better UX.
- Batching: best for background/async tasks — amortizes compute and reduces $/1M tokens but increases tail latency; not ideal for <250ms SLOs.
- Hybrid approach: host top-3 journeys on low-latency tier (or Dedicated small pool) with streaming + commit to cache; route background workloads to a batched cheaper pool.

Next steps I’ll bring to the Wed meeting:
- Finalized price band + sample contract language for Dedicated (term options).
- A small benchmark deck showing p95 at sample configs (batch sizes, streaming on/off).

Attaching: redwood-pricing-math.xlsx (summary tab) and redwood-latency-benchmarks.pdf.

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Daniel / team —

Quick technical addendum on options and unit math so you have something to review before Wed:

Assumptions (for the example below): generative = 20M tokens/mo; embeddings = 3M tokens/mo.

Dedicated example (recommended for strict p95):
- Config: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool), quantized model, KV cache enabled for repeated prefixes, streaming enabled for low latency.
- Expected p95: ~180–260ms for common turn sizes (depends on prompt length).
- Cost math (rough): infra + infra-ops amortized -> equivalent ~$11.5 / 1M generative tokens. Embeddings typically charged separately (~$6 / 1M embeddings) — see attached workbook for line items.

Hosted low-latency tier example:
- Config: managed low-latency tier with autoscaled instances; streaming encouraged.
- Expected p95: ~120–300ms depending on load and bursts.
- Cost math (rough): ~$28 / 1M generative tokens at your volume due to higher instance/multitenant overhead and burst capacity pricing.

Trade-offs and recommendation:
- If FintechAI needs guaranteed sub-250ms p95 for the top-3 journeys and you expect sustained usage (~>15–20M tokens/mo), Dedicated is likely more cost-effective and predictable.
- If you want to pilot without commit, start on Hosted low-latency tier (we can support an interim SLO) and evaluate usage curves over 6–8 weeks, then convert to Dedicated with a True-up/rollback clause in the contract.

SLO-driven pricing option (we offer):
- Hybrid: base reserved capacity priced like Dedicated + overage billed at hosted rate. Optional SLO credit structure for missed p95 targets. We can draft a simple SLO clause for your procurement team.

I’ll bring a short benchmark snapshot to Wed with p95 curves for both configs.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
